title: schema-anchored-stream-assertor-and-token-guided-decoding-probes
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Goal: validate and harden streaming JSON-mode behavior when interleaved with tool/function-calls and partial token emissions. This ticket implements a test harness and assertor that uses short sentinel anchors plus token-guided decoding probes to exercise decoder gating, partial-emission recovery, and schema reconciliation across model variants and quantization profiles.

Rationale: existing suites focus on full-message post-hoc validation. In production streaming and tool-calls, partial payloads arrive incrementally and tool outputs can interleave with the JSON payload. We need deterministic probes that (1) assert schema prefix invariants mid-stream, (2) inject token-level adversarial emissions, and (3) verify graceful fallback and repair strategies (e.g., resync by sentinel, request-time retry of finalization, or fallback to truncated-object heuristics).
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs 1k randomized stream sessions against model variants (float16, int8, q4_x) with deterministic seed and reports a schema-violation rate per variant.
Mid-stream sentinel anchors detected and used to resynchronize > 95% of otherwise out-of-sync partial JSON emissions in < 200ms median recovery time.

Tool/function-call interleavings simulated: for 3 common tool patterns (single tool return, streaming tool chunks, nested toolcalls) the decoder gate avoids mis-attribution of tool payload into JSON > 99% of trials.
A documented runbook for developer teams that describes remediation paths (retry, switch to strict-json finalizer, or use post-emit reconciliation) and when to enable them.
Telemetry surfaced to Console: per-request schema-failure, recovery-latency, decoder-backoff-events, and variant breakdowns.
Automated CI coverage added and green on runtime-1.26 branch; no regressions on existing structured-output smoke suites.
test_plan: Implement stream-assertor harness (python) that opens a streaming session, injects a small JSON template, and inserts sentinel tokens at deterministic positions.
Create token-guided adversary that forces partial-token corruptions: truncation, extra-punctuation, unclosed braces, and toolcall-mock interleaving.
Run matrix of model variants x payload shapes x toolcall patterns x quantization profiles; collect structured metrics and raw transcripts.
Add a unit for the constrained-decoder shim to verify it enforces prefix grammar without blocking streaming throughput beyond 5% latency overhead.
Integrate harness into CI with a "smoke-fast" subset and a nightly heavy fuzz run that uploads artifacts to the artifact bucket for debugging.
Finalize tests that verify compatibility layer behavior when downgraded models are routed (e.g., strict->relaxed schema modes) and ensure graceful degradation acceptance criteria are met.
telemetry: schema_violation_rate: count per 1000 requests by model_variant
toolcall_interference_rate: fraction of sessions where tool output overlapped JSON payload
fuzz_case_bucket: labels for failure taxonomy (truncation, garble, injection, tool-overlap)
comments: 2026-02-16 - Initial spike completed: validated sentinel approach against small Llama variant. Found that naive sentinel tokens were echoed by some models; we added an escaping sentinel scheme.

2026-02-20 - Prototype harness assembled. First matrix run uncovered a regression with q4_x variant where prefix gating added ~12% latency; engineering experiment to push gating to async validator started.
2026-02-24 - Design review with PM and DX: agreed to include explicit developer controls in Console to toggle 'strict-finalizer' and to surface recovery suggestions inline with failed traces.
2026-02-28 - PR opened for harness and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-assertor/pull/182 (needs runtime perf sign-off).
2026-03-01 - Blocker: need updated kernel-selection profile from runtime infra to measure true latency impact on Dedicated; reaching out to infra owners (tagging ENG-612345).
notes: Trade-offs considered: stronger in-line gating reduces schema failures but increases tail latency for small requests; we prioritized a sentinel+async-validate hybrid to balance. Also evaluated approach of leveraging function-calling metadata to demarcate tool output vs JSON payload, but not all models honor toolcall annotations consistently, so the harness treats toolcall sequences as adversarial inputs and verifies decoder resilience.
